title: Quasi-isomorphism criterion for colimits of free representable function resolutions
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small subcanonical site with finite products [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, and use ordinary $R$-module sheaves and cochain derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $U$ for the underlying abelian sheaf, $\iota$ for inclusion of abelian sheaves into presheaves, $a$ for abelian sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], and $t_P(A)(V)=A(V\times P)$ for a fixed $P\in\mathcal C$. Let $R[P]$ be the free module sheaf on the representable $h_P$ and put $H_P=\mathcal Hom_R(R[P],-)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Let $I$ be a small filtered category and $M:I\to\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ have colimit $M_\infty$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Supply a compatible diagram $M_i[0]\to K_i$ of nonnegative injective resolutions, a nonnegative injective resolution $M_\infty[0]\to K_\infty$, and a cocone $k_i:K_i\to K_\infty$ whose composites with augmentations equal the original module coprojections followed by the last augmentation [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Put $c:\operatorname{colim}_iH_P(K_i)\to H_P(K_\infty)$ for the induced chain map. Let $\delta:\operatorname{colim}_i R\iota(UM_i[0])\to R\iota(UM_\infty[0])$ be the derived-presheaf comparison induced by those coprojections. Every filtered colimit here is the localization of a compatible termwise complex colimit, or equivalently its exact derived functor. If $\delta$ is an isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{PAb}(\mathcal C))$, then $c$ is a quasi-isomorphism, and hence $Q(c)$ is invertible in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(R))$. More precisely, write $h^q(F)=H^q(R\iota(F[0]))$. The map $H^q(Uc)$ is identified, naturally in the coefficient cocone, with
$$a\,t_P\!\left(\operatorname{colim}_i h^q(UM_i)\longrightarrow h^q(UM_\infty)\right).$$
The arrow inside parentheses is $H^q(\delta)$ under the exact filtered-colimit identification; it is induced by the original module coprojections, and negative degrees are zero. The identifications used here are the cohomology of the derived-category isomorphisms of [lem-sfb-free-representable-derived-functions-model], not an assumed lift of those isomorphisms to a diagram of complexes. The criterion and its comparison normalization hold for every augmentation-compatible choice of the supplied resolutions, naturally for compatible coefficient maps and contravariantly in $P$. No finite-cover or cohomological-dimension hypothesis is required, and no assertion that $R\iota$ always preserves filtered colimits is made.

proof.text: The functor $U$ is exact and commutes with small colimits by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]; $a$ is exact and commutes with colimits by [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact]. Precomposition $t_P$ is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-presheaves-evaluation-exact], applied at $V\times P$, and commutes with colimits by [lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-colimits-sectionwise], evaluated at that same object. Filtered colimits of abelian sheaves are exact by [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaves-filtered-colimits-exact]. Filtered colimits of abelian presheaves are exact by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-abelian-groups-exact] and [lem-weil-pbc-functor-exact-colimits], with functor index $\mathcal C^{op}$. All these indices are small. Thus [src-weil-homology-preserves-exact-colimits] applies in both abelian categories. Exactness and faithfulness of $U$ also imply exactness of filtered module colimits: their underlying sequences are the exact abelian-sheaf colimits, and zero kernel modulo image is detected by $U$.

proof.text:
Write $r_i:M_i[0]\to K_i$ and $r_\infty:M_\infty[0]\to K_\infty$ for the supplied augmentations; they are quasi-isomorphisms. By [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective](1),(2), the comparison $\alpha_{K}:Q(H_P(K))\to RH_P(QK)$ is natural in bounded-below complexes $K$ and invertible on complexes of injectives. Put $\varepsilon_i=RH_P(Q(r_i))^{-1}\alpha_{K_i}:Q(H_P(K_i))\cong RH_P(M_i[0])$ and likewise $\varepsilon_\infty$. For a module map $f$ and a supplied chain map $g$ with $g\circ r=r'\circ f[0]$ (a transition map of the diagram or a cocone map $k_i$), naturality of $\alpha$ gives $\varepsilon'Q(H_P(g))=RH_P(f[0])\varepsilon$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] $U$ is exact, so [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] gives $D(U)Q(H_P(K_i))\cong Q(UH_P(K_i))$ naturally; $a$ and $t_P$ are exact (step 1) and the same node with [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] gives $H^q(D(a)D(t_P)Y)\cong a t_PH^q(Y)$, first for $Y=QL$ and then for all $Y$, naturally in $Y$ since both sides invert quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Composing these with $H^q(D(U)\varepsilon_i)$ and $H^q$ of the canonical isomorphism $\Phi_{M_i}:D(U)RH_P(M_i[0])\cong D(a)D(t_P)R\iota(UM_i[0])$ of [lem-sfb-free-representable-derived-functions-model] gives
$$\beta_i^q:H^q(UH_P(K_i))\cong a t_Ph^q(UM_i),$$
and likewise $\beta_\infty^q$. By construction these are the cohomology of the derived isomorphisms of that node, read off its statement; no isomorphism of derived objects is lifted to a complex diagram. The naturality of $\Phi$ for module maps and the identities above make the $\beta_i^q$ compatible with the transition maps of the supplied diagram.

proof.text:
Use $U$-colimit preservation from [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] and exact-colimit homology from [src-weil-homology-preserves-exact-colimits], with the exactness established in step 1. They give
$$H^q(U\operatorname{colim}_iH_P(K_i))\cong\operatorname{colim}_iH^q(UH_P(K_i)).$$
Apply the colimit of the maps $\beta_i^q$ of step 2. Since $a$ commutes with colimits [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact] and $t_P$ does so sectionwise [lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-colimits-sectionwise], the result is
$$H^q(U\operatorname{colim}_iH_P(K_i))\cong a t_P\operatorname{colim}_ih^q(UM_i).$$
Every displayed identification uses the canonical colimit coprojections; no presheaf colimit is being identified with a sheaf colimit without sheafification.

proof.text:
Let $m_i:M_i\to M_\infty$ be a coefficient coprojection. The augmentation condition says $k_i\circ r_i=r_\infty\circ m_i[0]$, so step 2 gives $\varepsilon_\infty Q(H_P(k_i))=RH_P(m_i[0])\varepsilon_i$. By [lem-sfb-free-representable-derived-functions-model], $\Phi_{M_\infty}\circ D(U)RH_P(m_i[0])=D(a)D(t_P)R\iota(Um_i[0])\circ\Phi_{M_i}$. The comparisons $D(U)Q\cong QU$ of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] and the cohomology comparisons of step 2, which rest on [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology], are natural. Hence
$$\beta_\infty^q H^q(UH_P(k_i))=a t_PH^q(R\iota(Um_i[0]))\beta_i^q.$$
Since $c$ composed with the $i$-th coprojection is $H_P(k_i)$, step 3 makes $H^q(Uc)$ equal to $a t_P$ of the unique map $\operatorname{colim}_ih^q(UM_i)\to h^q(UM_\infty)$ with components $H^q(R\iota(Um_i[0]))$: check the equality after every coprojection and use [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. This map is $H^q(\delta)$: $\delta$ composed with the $i$-th coprojection of the derived colimit is $R\iota(Um_i[0])$, and [src-weil-homology-preserves-exact-colimits], with the presheaf exactness of step 1, identifies $H^q$ of that colimit with $\operatorname{colim}_ih^q(UM_i)$ through those coprojections. This proves the requested normalization, including the actual cocone map rather than only its source and target objects.

source.place: Tag 013P (lemma-morphisms-lift) for the augmentation-compatible maps; agent cocone calculation through the naturality clause of the cited derived free-representable model.

proof.text: If $\delta$ is invertible, every $H^q(\delta)$ is invertible because cohomology is a functor on the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Step 4 and functoriality of $a t_P$ make $H^q(Uc)$ invertible. Exactness of $U$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] identify this with $U(H^q(c))$. An inverse to an underlying abelian-sheaf isomorphism of modules is $R$-linear: for $f$ linear, $f(rf^{-1}(y))=ry=f(f^{-1}(ry))$, and injectivity gives equality. Thus each $H^q(c)$ is invertible. By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $c$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $Q(c)$ is invertible. Negative degrees vanish because all supplied complexes, their Hom complexes and their termwise colimits are nonnegative. The argument of steps 2-4 applies verbatim to any augmentation-compatible choice of resolutions. For a compatible map of coefficient diagrams, augmentation-compatible lifts exist and are unique up to homotopy by [lem-sfb-module-resolution-derived-presheaf-comparison]; the identity of step 2 for $\varepsilon$, the covariant naturality of $\Phi$ in $M$ and its contravariant naturality in $P$ from [lem-sfb-free-representable-derived-functions-model], and the naturality of the cohomology comparisons in the exact functor ($t_P\to t_{P'}$ is restriction along $1_V\times u$, which preserves kernels and images) make the $\beta$ squares commute. Taking cohomology and colimits preserves these equalities, proving all the stated naturalities and choice independence. The argument used no covering finiteness or cohomological bound.
